places.name: Lisboa
past: The lords built their castle on the hill above the town, where it could watch the roads for leagues.
Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit runs wide of the old; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line.
A great fire burned 23 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the northern side; 0 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 9 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.

Walled, the river and the lie of the land sparing a stretch of the circuit.

places.name: Marvila
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 85% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line; 2 houses were built into what was left of it.
A great fire burned 15 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The Franciscans were given ground by the wall for their friary.
A great fire burned 25 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
